target: Gwahododd nhw ni i'r briodas.
english: They invited us to the wedding.
tip: Object pronouns follow the verb and subject: Gwahododd nhw ni = they invited us. nhw is subject, ni object.

target: Gwlad y gân yw Cymru.
english: Wales is the land of song.
tip: Welsh shows of by stacking nouns with y between them: Gwlad y gân means land of the song.

target: Cenir y gân mewn gemau rygbi.
english: The song is sung at rugby matches.
tip: The -ir ending is a passive with no named doer: Cenir means is sung.

target: Mae'r haf yn gynhesach na'r gwanwyn.
english: The summer is warmer than the spring.
tip: The -ach ending makes comparatives, and na means than: gynhesach na means warmer than.

target: Mae tri pheth ar y rhestr.
english: There are three things on the list.
tip: tri (three) triggers aspirate mutation: peth becomes pheth. tri pheth means three things.

target: Nabyddais i mohoni hi ar y dechrau.
english: I didn't recognise her at first.
tip: To negate a definite object, Welsh uses mo plus a pronoun ending. mo + hi becomes mohoni (not her).

target: Dechreuodd y cyngerdd am wyth o'r gloch.
english: The concert started at eight o'clock.
tip: Clock times use o'r gloch, literally 'of the bell': am wyth o'r gloch = at eight o'clock. am marks 'at'.

target: Mae ei mam hi'n pobi'r bara gorau.
english: Her mother bakes the best bread.
tip: The echo hi shows ei means her, not his: ei mam hi is her mother.

target: Enillodd hi'r wobr gyntaf yn y sioe.
english: She won first prize at the show.
tip: Adjectives soft-mutate after a feminine noun: cyntaf becomes gyntaf. y wobr gyntaf = the first prize.

target: Roedd wyth gwestai wrth y bwrdd cinio.
english: There were eight guests at the dinner table.
tip: Nouns stay singular after a number: wyth gwestai is literally eight guest, not guests.

target: Dysgais i nofio pan oeddwn i'n bump.
english: I learned to swim when I was five.
tip: dysgu covers both learning and teaching. Here Dysgais i nofio means I learned to swim.

target: Roedd chwe ystafell yn ein hen dŷ.
english: We had six rooms in our old house.
tip: hen (old) comes before its noun and softens it: tŷ turns into hen dŷ.

target: Mae fy ewythr yn ffermio yng ngogledd Cymru.
english: My uncle farms in north Wales.
tip: yn becomes yng before g, and gogledd becomes ngogledd: yng ngogledd means in the north of.

target: Allwch chi siarad yn arafach, os gwelwch yn dda?
english: Can you speak more slowly, please?
tip: Allwch chi ...? is a polite way to ask can you: Allwch chi siarad means can you speak.

target: Roedd un ar ddeg o chwaraewyr yn y tîm.
english: There were eleven players on the team.
tip: Eleven is un ar ddeg, literally one on ten, from the older base-twenty counting system.

target: Mae'r trên yn cyrraedd am ugain munud i bedwar.
english: The train arrives at twenty to four.
tip: i means to when telling time: ugain munud i bedwar is twenty minutes to four.

target: Clywodd Dewi gân hyfryd yn yr eglwys ddydd Sul.
english: Dewi heard a lovely song at church on Sunday.
tip: 'On a day' is shown by a soft mutation, with no word for 'on': dydd becomes ddydd. ddydd Sul = on Sunday.

target: Dywedodd y tywysydd fod y castell yn saith can mlwydd oed.
english: The guide said the castle was seven hundred years old.
tip: can (hundred) triggers a nasal mutation on the next word: blwydd becomes mlwydd. saith can mlwydd oed = 700 years old.

target: Roedd y cynllun peilot yn llwyddiannus mewn tri sir.
english: The pilot scheme was successful in three counties.
tip: Use mewn for in a or some (indefinite) and yn for in the (definite): mewn tri sir.

target: Golchodd Owain ei ddwylo cyn bwyta cinio.
english: Owain washed his hands before eating lunch.
tip: ei meaning 'his' soft-mutates the next word: dwylo becomes ddwylo. ei ddwylo = his hands.

target: Trowch i dudalen deg.
english: Turn to page ten.
tip: The -wch ending makes a command to chi, formal or group: Trowch means turn. Compare Eisteddwch, sit down, and Edrychwch, look.

target: Mae heddiw'n well na ddoe.
english: Today is better than yesterday.
tip: well is the irregular comparative of da, good. na means than: heddiw'n well na ddoe, today is better than yesterday.

target: Mae heddiw'n oerach na ddoe.
english: Today is colder than yesterday.
tip: Add -ach to an adjective for the comparative: oer, cold, becomes oerach, colder. na after it means than.

target: Mae fy nhaid yn hoffi garddio.
english: My grandfather likes gardening.
tip: fy, my, triggers nasal mutation: taid, grandfather, becomes fy nhaid. The t turns to nh.

target: Mae'r terfyn cyflymder yn dri deg.
english: The speed limit is thirty.
tip: Welsh builds tens as a unit plus deg, ten: dri deg is thirty, literally three tens.

target: Mae'r llong yn gadael am chwech.
english: The ship leaves at six.
tip: Use am for clock times: am chwech means at six. am can also mean for or about.

target: Mae fy mhlant yn tyfu'n gyflym.
english: My children are growing fast.
tip: Placing yn before an adjective makes it adverbial: cyflym, fast, softens to gyflym, meaning fast or quickly.

target: Mae fy nghefnder yn ddeg oed.
english: My cousin is ten years old.
tip: Give age with oed after a number: yn ddeg oed is ten years old, literally ten age.

target: Sylwais i fod y drws ar agor.
english: I noticed the door was open.
tip: The 'that' in a reported clause is bod, softened to fod here: Sylwais i fod y drws ar agor.

target: Enillodd ein tîm ni'r cwpan ddydd Sadwrn diwethaf.
english: Our team won the cup last Saturday.
tip: Wrap 'our' around the noun for emphasis: ein tîm ni = our team, with ni echoing the possessive ein.
